title: Phase 2 Evaluation of Recombinant Human Platelet-Derived Growth Factor-BB (rhPDGF-BB) Injection for the Treatment of Infraorbital Hollowing
official: A Multicenter, Phase 2 Randomized, Dose-Ranging and Pharmacokinetic Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Preliminary Efficacy of Recombinant Human Platelet-Derived Growth Factor-BB (rhPDGF-BB) Injection for the Treatment of Infraorbital Hollowing
summary:
The goal of this Phase 2 clinical trial is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary effectiveness of recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor-BB (rhPDGF-BB) injections for the treatment of moderate to severe infraorbital hollowing (under-eye hollows) in adults aged 21 to 65 years. The study is intended to evaluate the:

* Safety and tolerability of rhPDGF-BB following injections in the infraorbital area
* Preliminary efficacy (responder rate) of rhPDGF-BB compared with placebo
* Effect of different doses of rhPDGF-BB compared with placebo with respect to treatment response and durability
* Pharmacokinetic profile following injection of rhPDGF-BB in the infraorbital region
* Immunogenicity profile following injection of rhPDGF-BB in the infraorbital region

This study will compare two doses of rhPDGF-BB (37.5 µg and 75 µg per infraorbital region) with placebo (normal saline) to evaluate safety and preliminary efficacy of rhPDGF-BB for improving infraorbital hollowing.

Participants will:

* Receive injections of rhPDGF-BB or placebo in the infraorbital area.
* Attend follow-up visits for safety and assessment of changes in infraorbital hollowing.
* Undergo clinical grading and standardized facial imaging and complete questionnaires about treatment outcomes and satisfaction.
* Provide blood samples for assessment of drug exposure and immune response to rhPDGF-BB.
* Be evaluated for possible retreatment at Week 8 according to the study protocol and followed for up to 24 weeks after their final treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults 21 to 65 years of age.
* Moderate to severe infraorbital hollowing, defined as a Canfield Infraorbital Hollow Severity Scale (CIOHS) score ≥3; mild orbital fat ptosis is permitted if, in the investigator's judgment, the condition is amenable to treatment.
* Fitzpatrick skin type I-VI.
* Willing and able to comply with study visits and photography requirements and provide written informed consent.
* Willing to refrain from other aesthetic treatments in the infraorbital region for the duration of the study.
* Women of childbearing potential must have a negative pregnancy test at screening and agree to use a highly effective method of contraception from screening through 24 weeks after the final treatment. Acceptable methods include methods with a failure rate of \<1% per year when used consistently and correctly (e.g., hormonal contraception, intrauterine device/system, bilateral tubal occlusion, or sexual abstinence consistent with the participant's lifestyle). Women of childbearing potential must not be pregnant or breastfeeding.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior or planned during the study period dermal fillers, fat grafting, other injectable treatments, or aesthetic procedures in the infraorbital region.
* Significant orbital fat herniation, skin laxity, or anatomical features that may confound assessment of infraorbital hollowing.
* Prior surgical procedures in the infraorbital or periorbital region (e.g., blepharoplasty).
* Lower-lid surgery (blepharoplasty) within 12 months or unresolved sequelae.
* Active dermatologic disease, inflammation, or infection in the treatment area.
* Autoimmune or connective tissue disease, immunosuppression, or other uncontrolled systemic disease (e.g., diabetes) judged to increase risk, affect healing, or otherwise affect study outcomes.
* Known hypersensitivity to study product components or to local anesthetics used per protocol, including allergy to yeast-derived products.
* History of abnormal wound healing (e.g., keloids or hypertrophic scarring).
* Currently pregnant or breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during the study.
* Clinically significant ophthalmologic conditions that may confound safety assessments, including but not limited to visual acuity not corrected to at least 20/40, active glaucoma, severe dry eye disease, diabetic retinopathy, history of ocular surgery within 12 months, retinal or vascular ocular disease, or active ocular infection or inflammation.
* Any medical history, condition, or prior procedure affecting the anatomy, appearance, or function of the infraorbital area, periorbital structures, orbital contents, nose, or mid-face that, in the investigator's judgment, would confound assessment of study treatment safety or efficacy or pose increased procedural risk. This includes, but is not limited to, prior orbital trauma or fracture, prior orbital or periorbital surgery, active or recurrent periorbital infections or inflammatory dermatoses, systemic anticoagulation or bleeding disorders, and active autoimmune or connective tissue diseases.
* Concurrent use of prescription or nonprescription products with known or suspected growth-factor-mediated effects within protocol-defined washout periods that may confound efficacy assessment.
* Use of anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, or medications that may increase bleeding risk, unless stable and medically appropriate.
* Participation in another clinical trial within the protocol-defined period before screening.
* Known, untreated malignant neoplasm(s) at the treatment site(s) or currently undergoing radiation therapy or chemotherapy.
